newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan uses privatisation money to retire debt.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan uses privatisation money to retire debt.

text.p: The State (Central) Bank of Pakistan (SBP) said on Friday it had used 1.5 billion rupees from privatisation of a state-owned bank to retire domestic debt on Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif's instructions.

The proceeds from this month's sale of a 70 percent stake in Habib Credit and Exchange Bank Ltd (HCEBL), were used to retire debt amounting to 1.5 billion rupees which carried an interest rate of 17.29 percent a year, an SBP statement said.
"The State Bank intends to make public whenever privatisation proceeds are received and used for debt retirement," it said.
"The SBP will ensure that, unlike in the past, the retirement of debt under the scheme does not increase the scope for additional government borrowing from the banking system."
"The Prime Minister of Pakistan has directed the State Bank to ensure that all privatisation proceeds are used for the retirement of the most expensive debt," the statement added.

A consortium led by a United Arab Emirates businessman bought the HCEBL shares after bidding 39 rupees a share for the 42 million shares on June 12. HCEBL was once part of the collapsed Bank of Credit and Commerce International (BCCI).
Pakistan's domestic debt will total one trillion (1,000 billion) rupees at the end of fiscal 1996/97 (July-June) according to budget estimates.
